blocks.content: Every High Court shall be a court of record and shall have all the powers of such a court including the power to punish for contempt of itself.

rows: Contempt of itself and any court or tribunal across India
Contempt of itself and courts subordinate to it within its territorial jurisdiction
Binding on all courts within the territory of India
Binding on all subordinate courts within its respective state/jurisdiction

items: Article 215 pertains to the High Court as a Court of Record, whereas Article 129 confers the same status on the Supreme Court.
High Courts have the jurisdiction to punish for contempt of themselves as well as courts subordinate to them.
The constitutional power to punish for contempt under Article 215 cannot be taken away or limited even by statutory legislation.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 215 designates every High Court in India as a Court of Record.
The judgments, records, and proceedings of the High Court are preserved for perpetual memory and evidentiary testimony.
Acts as a Court of Record grants the High Court the inherent constitutional power to punish for contempt of itself.
Records of a High Court possess unquestionable evidentiary value and cannot be challenged when produced in subordinate courts.
